title: Krishna Sets the Hill Down
story:
The storm had ended, and the cowherds came out from beneath the hill into a world that seemed new. Each one gathered up what was his — the goods they had carried into the shelter, the cattle that had waited out the deluge with them — and they looked around at the washed land and the returned sun. For seven days they had been hidden away in the dim hollow beneath the mountain, and now the sky was clear and the ground was solid beneath their feet again. There was a quiet gladness in the simple act of stepping out, of feeling the rain gone and the light return. The fear they had carried all that week went out of them like a held breath finally released.

Then Krishna, who had held Govardhana above them for seven days without moving, set the mountain back down. He placed it in its own place, as it had stood before, and let his arm rest. The great hill that had hung over their heads like a roof settled back onto the earth as though it had never moved, and the land that had sheltered them closed over the gap where they had hidden. Nothing about the hill had changed; it stood where it had always stood, and only the memory of those seven days remained.

What followed was not ceremony but embrace. Nanda, his father, came to him, and Yashoda, his mother, and Rohini, and Balarama, strongest of the strong. They gathered around Krishna with an affection that had been held back too long, and they embraced him. For seven days they had watched him stand alone beneath the weight of a mountain, and now that it was over, holding him close was the first thing they could think to do. The cowherds pressed close and surrounded him, and the gopis came with their honor, welcoming him with curd and unbroken rice and showering blessings on him with glad hearts. What the storm had scattered, the love of the village now gathered back together, and for a little while there was no distance between the boy and the people who had feared for him.

And the rejoicing did not stay on the ground. In heaven the hosts of the gods had been watching — the siddhas and the sadhyas, the gandharvas and the charanas — and now, stirred to praise, they rained flowers down upon him. Conches and drums sounded in the sky. The very heavens that had sent the storm now sent down a softer answer, petals instead of hail and music instead of thunder.

Then Krishna, surrounded by the devoted cowherds, set out with Balarama for his own cow-pen. And Vrindavan was quiet again, in the way a place is quiet after a great thing has passed through it and gone home.
reflection: The ending restores everything the storm had broken: the hill to its place, the family to its embrace, and the sky itself from wrath to praise. The gods who sent the rain now send flowers, and the rejoicing on the ground is answered from above.
next_story_tease: But the king of the gods had not finished with Vrindavan; he would come down himself to make amends.
hero_scene: Krishna lowering Govardhana back into its place as the sun returns, while Nanda, Yashoda, Rohini, and Balarama embrace him and flowers rain down from heaven amid the sound of conches and drums.
